def count_cycle_covers(grid, k):
    """Count the ways to cover all free cells of a rectangular grid by
    exactly k vertex-disjoint simple cycles.

    Input: grid is a list of 1 to 6 strings, all of the same length between
    1 and 8, made only of '.' (free cell) and '#' (blocked cell); k is an
    int with 0 <= k <= 4.

    A simple cycle is a closed tour c_1, c_2, ..., c_L (L >= 4) of pairwise
    distinct free cells in which consecutive cells, and also c_L and c_1,
    are orthogonal (side-sharing) neighbours.  A cycle is unoriented and
    has no distinguished starting cell: it is identified with its set of L
    edges.  A valid configuration is a set of exactly k cycles that are
    pairwise vertex-disjoint and whose cells together cover every free
    cell of the grid exactly once (blocked cells are covered by none).
    Two configurations are the same if and only if the unions of their
    edge sets are equal.

    Return the number of valid configurations as an int.  If the grid has
    no free cells, the empty configuration is the unique cover, so the
    answer is 1 if k == 0 and 0 otherwise.  If there is at least one free
    cell, k == 0 yields 0.  Whenever no valid configuration exists the
    answer is 0.

    Bounds: 1 <= rows <= 6, 1 <= columns <= 8, 0 <= k <= 4.  Enumerating
    edge subsets (up to 2^82) or cell tours is astronomically slow even at
    this size.

    >>> count_cycle_covers(['..', '..'], 1)
    1
    >>> count_cycle_covers(['....', '....', '....', '....'], 1)
    6
    >>> count_cycle_covers(['....', '....'], 2)
    1
    >>> count_cycle_covers(['...', '.#.', '...'], 1)
    1
    """
